questions.question: Choose one project from your resume. What problem did it solve, what did you personally own, and how did you know it was useful?
strong_signals: states a concrete responsibility
connects an outcome to a metric or user need

questions.question: Walk me through the path from raw input to prediction in your project. Where did validation and error handling happen?
strong_signals: explains the full data flow
identifies a realistic failure case
weak_signals: jumps directly from input to output

questions.question: What input or model failure worried you most in that system, and how would you detect and handle it safely?
strong_signals: names a concrete failure
proposes detection before mitigation

questions.question: How did you split training, validation, and test data, and what leakage risk did you check for?
strong_signals: explains why the split matches the data
identifies a leakage path

questions.question: If the important class was rare, how would you measure whether the model was really helping rather than just predicting the majority class?
strong_signals: rejects accuracy as the only metric
connects metric choice to the cost of errors
weak_signals: cannot distinguish false positives and false negatives

questions.question: Which metric mattered most for your classifier, and why was it better than accuracy for that decision?
strong_signals: ties the metric to the real decision
explains the cost of a false positive or false negative

questions.question: How would changing the prediction threshold affect precision and recall, and how would you choose a threshold for a real user?
strong_signals: describes the trade-off correctly
uses validation or cost to choose the threshold

questions.question: In your PyTorch training loop, what happened in one epoch from loading a batch through updating the model?
strong_signals: explains the order correctly
mentions train and evaluation modes when relevant

questions.question: What evidence would tell you the model was overfitting, and which intervention would you try first?
strong_signals: uses validation behavior as evidence
chooses an intervention with a reason

questions.question: For an image classifier with limited labelled data, when would you use transfer learning and which layers would you fine-tune first?
strong_signals: explains why early features transfer
describes a staged fine-tuning plan

questions.question: How did you decide which input features were useful, and how did you make sure preprocessing was applied consistently at inference time?
strong_signals: avoids fitting preprocessing on test data
explains feature value
weak_signals: preprocessing differs between training and inference

questions.question: How would you choose chunk size and overlap for a RAG system, and what trade-off would you expect?
strong_signals: connects chunking to document structure and retrieval
recognises recall versus noise
weak_signals: assumes bigger chunks are always better

questions.question: How would you tell whether poor answers came from retrieval, the prompt, or the language model itself?
strong_signals: separates pipeline components
proposes representative evaluation cases
weak_signals: has no way to inspect retrieved context

questions.question: What guardrails would you put around an LLM feature before showing its output to a user?
strong_signals: covers both input and output
explains a failure path
weak_signals: relies only on the system prompt
assumes a model refusal is enough

questions.question: How would you package a trained model for an API, and what inputs would you validate before running inference?
strong_signals: separates training artifact from service
validates shape and type
weak_signals: loads a notebook directly in production

questions.question: After deployment, which signals would you monitor to catch performance or data drift before users report a problem?
strong_signals: includes service and model metrics
explains how labels or feedback close the loop

questions.question: Tell me about a model result that looked wrong. What did you check first, and how did you narrow down the cause?
strong_signals: uses a systematic sequence
starts with data or reproducibility

questions.question: How would you explain a model limitation to a non-technical stakeholder without hiding the risk?
strong_signals: balances clarity and honesty
offers an actionable mitigation

questions.question: Can you explain the difference between compile-time and runtime polymorphism with a concrete example?
strong_signals: distinguishes overloading from overriding accurately
explains dynamic method dispatch at runtime

questions.question: Why is 'composition over inheritance' widely recommended in system design, and when would inheritance be a poor choice?
strong_signals: mentions tight coupling or fragile base class problem
explains runtime flexibility of composition
weak_signals: claims inheritance is always better for code reuse

questions.question: Walk me through how the Open-Closed Principle or Liskov Substitution Principle prevents regression bugs in large codebases.
strong_signals: explains extending behavior without modifying source code
demonstrates breaking LSP with unexpected subclass behavior
weak_signals: simply recites the acronym without architectural intuition

questions.question: How does the JVM distinguish between Stack and Heap memory, and what causes an OutOfMemoryError versus a StackOverflowError?
strong_signals: explains method frames and primitives on stack vs objects on heap
connects deep recursion to stack overflow and memory leaks to OOM
weak_signals: believes garbage collection frees stack frames

questions.question: How does Java's HashMap work internally, how are collisions resolved, and why is the equals and hashCode contract critical?
strong_signals: explains bucketing, linked list chaining, and treeify conversion at threshold 8
details what happens when hashCode is inconsistent with equals
weak_signals: cannot explain why equals is needed after hashcode match

questions.question: What is the key difference between the volatile keyword and synchronized blocks in Java multithreading?
strong_signals: articulates that volatile guarantees memory visibility but not atomicity
explains mutual exclusion with synchronized
weak_signals: thinks volatile makes operations like count++ atomic

questions.question: What is Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), and why does multithreading not speed up CPU-bound workloads in CPython?
strong_signals: explains reference counting safety and GIL mutex
recommends multiprocessing or asyncio depending on CPU vs I/O bound tasks
weak_signals: assumes threads always run on multiple CPU cores in Python

questions.question: How do Python generators work with the yield statement, and why are they preferable to lists for large-scale data pipelines?
strong_signals: explains memory footprint reduction and lazy evaluation
describes how yield suspends execution state and frame
weak_signals: does not mention memory or lazy streaming

questions.question: How does a B-Tree index speed up SELECT queries in MySQL, and what is the trade-off when performing heavy INSERT or UPDATE operations?
strong_signals: explains log(N) search and leaf node lookup
notes that writes suffer due to index tree rebalancing and page splits
weak_signals: thinks indexes speed up both reads and writes
cannot explain how an index structures data

questions.question: Can you explain the difference between Read Committed and Repeatable Read isolation levels, and what anomalies each prevents?
strong_signals: clearly explains dirty reads vs non-repeatable reads
mentions multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) or snapshots
weak_signals: recites ACID without knowing what isolation levels mean

questions.question: Why is hash table lookup O(1) on average, but what causes it to degrade to O(N), and how do you prevent that?
strong_signals: explains hash collision clustering and load factor threshold triggering rehashing
mentions good hash distribution function
weak_signals: thinks hash tables are always strictly O(1) with no worst case

questions.question: How would you design a Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache so that both get() and put() run in O(1) time?
strong_signals: combines HashMap for O(1) lookup with Doubly Linked List for O(1) removal and insertion at head/tail
explains node pointer updates on access
weak_signals: proposes array or queue leading to O(N) search or shift
fails to achieve O(1) for both get and put

questions.question: How would you detect a cycle in a linked list in linear time and constant extra memory?
strong_signals: describes Floyd's tortoise and hare pointers
explains why they must meet if a cycle exists
weak_signals: uses a hash set and extra memory

questions.question: Walk me through one web project on your resume. What did you personally build in the UI or API, and how did users hit it?
strong_signals: names concrete screens or endpoints they owned
weak_signals: only names the stack with no ownership

questions.question: How did you authenticate API requests in that app, and what happens when a token expires?
strong_signals: explains token lifecycle and a failure path
weak_signals: says login works with no detail

questions.question: How did you manage client state in the UI, and how did you avoid unnecessary re-renders?
strong_signals: mentions lifting state, context, or a store with a reason

questions.question: Tell me about a time you had to explain a sensitive update to a candidate or hiring manager. What did you say, and what was the outcome?
strong_signals: specific situation, action, and result
weak_signals: generic I am a good communicator

questions.question: Describe a disagreement between a hiring manager and a candidate process. How did you handle it without burning either side?
strong_signals: names the tension and a concrete step they took
weak_signals: says they stay positive with no example

questions.question: How do you decide whether a profile is a real match for a role versus a keyword match on the CV?
strong_signals: talks about evidence of skill, not just buzzwords

general: What was the hardest technical bug you encountered in this project and how did you track it down?
